0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Touraine is the heart of the Loire Valley, famous for châteaux, gastronomy and wine. Beyond the halo of Chinon and Vouvray, Touraine has a group of reds and rosés with distinct characters: from the regional Touraine Rouge, to Touraine-Amboise beside the château, to the one-of-a-kind three-Pinot blend — Touraine-Noble-Joué.

Learning Objectives

🗺️ Grasp the Touraine AOC hierarchy

Understand the varieties and style differences between regional Touraine and the village-level Touraine-Amboise and Touraine-Noble-Joué

🎭 Know one of France's most unusual rosé AOCs

Why Touraine-Noble-Joué must blend three Pinots, and the cultural meaning of this "grey rosé"

🍇 Understand the roles of Gamay and Côt (Malbec) in Touraine

How two unusual varieties found their place in Touraine
1.title: Touraine Rouge — The Backbone of Touraine's Regional Reds
1.highlights.0.content: A regional AOC covering all of Touraine. Gamay (main) + Cabernet Franc + Côt (Malbec) blend, light and fruity in style, suited to drinking young
1.highlights.1.content: A village-level AOC beside the Château d'Amboise, with red wine centred on Côt (Malbec) (the new INAO rules require 100% Côt; before the 2017 vintage a transition period allowed a little Gamay and Cabernet Franc), with more depth than regional Touraine
1.highlights.2.content: A regional rosé AOC, mainly Gamay, light and crisp, a good choice for everyday summer rosé
1.content:
Touraine Rouge is Touraine's most important red AOC, covering the broad Touraine region (excluding village-level appellations such as Chinon and Bourgueil).

🍇 The role of Gamay

A variety that came from Beaujolais, showing tighter acidity on Touraine's limestone soils. As the main variety, it gives Touraine Rouge fresh red-fruit aromas and a light drinking feel. "Gamay-Touraine" is a well-known regional brand.

🍇 The role of Côt (Malbec)

Malbec, called "Côt" in Touraine, is more refined than the Argentine version, with more violet florals and spice; a small amount in the blend adds depth of colour and aromatic complexity.

Touraine-Amboise is centred on the old town of Amboise; on tuffeau and sandy soils it makes reds from Côt (Malbec) with more character than the regional wines, and some can age 3–5 years.

3.title: Touraine-Noble-Joué — France's Strangest Rosé AOC
3.content:
Among all French AOCs, Touraine-Noble-Joué is one of the most unique: it is one of the very few French AOCs that mandates a blend of three grapes, and all three are of the Pinot family.

⚖️ Legal blending rules

Must blend: Pinot Meunier + Pinot Gris + Pinot Noir

The proportions of the three varieties are each regulated, so no single variety can dominate.

🌹 The mystery of the "Gris" colour

Noble-Joué is traditionally called vin gris (grey wine) — because of the grey-rose skins of Pinot Gris and the pale colour of Pinot Meunier, after winemaking it shows a coppery brown-grey between pink and pale red, a very distinctive visual effect.

🍷 Style character

Crisp, high acidity, with fresh aromas of raspberry, peach and ginger, and a fine spicy finish (from Pinot Meunier). Low alcohol and dry, a superb partner for a French lunch.

📜 Historical origins

Noble-Joué has over 500 years of history and was once the royal table wine of the French court in Touraine. It nearly disappeared in the mid-20th century, was revived by the local agricultural school in 1975, and today remains a small-production historical heritage.
4.title: Quiz
4.questions.0.question: Why is the blending rule of Touraine-Noble-Joué so special?
4.questions.0.options.0: It is the only AOC in France allowing only Gamay
4.questions.0.options.1: It mandates a blend of three Pinot-family varieties: Pinot Meunier + Pinot Gris + Pinot Noir
4.questions.0.options.2: It requires at least 50% Cabernet Franc
4.questions.0.options.3: It is France's oldest AOC, established in the 15th century
4.questions.0.explanation: Touraine-Noble-Joué is one of the very few French AOCs mandating a blend of three varieties, all of the Pinot family (Pinot Meunier, Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir), creating a unique "grey rosé (vin gris)" style with over 500 years of history.
4.questions.1.question: Which internationally known variety does the name Côt represent in Touraine?
4.questions.1.explanation: Côt is the traditional name for Malbec in the Loire Valley (especially Touraine and Anjou), the same variety as Argentina's Malbec, but in Touraine's cool climate the style is more refined and light, with violet and spice character.
